world.name: The Old Province

locations.name: Fox hollow
locations.description: A small settlement of hearth fires, kitchen gardens, and familiar faces. Ashfall fever has reached its households; the old shrine is still a place to seek help. Public necromantic practice is prohibited. Authorities require a witness or evidence before opening an investigation. A pear tree grows through the roof of the old toll house. The children use its branches as a lookout. An absent neighbor keeps a named place at the seasonal meal.
locations.localCustom: An absent neighbor keeps a named place at the seasonal meal.

institutions.name: Fox hollow Wren Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: Fox hollow Glass Shrine
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Leafsong
locations.description: The region’s busy city gathers an academy, a guild market, and a sworn order behind its stone walls. Fever wards are filling, and scholars disagree over the cause. Public necromantic practice is prohibited. Authorities require a witness or evidence before opening an investigation. On wash days, apprentices carry dyed cloth across the square; the Fox hollow carts wait until it dries. Repair work is witnessed before coin changes hands.
locations.localCustom: Repair work is witnessed before coin changes hands.

institutions.name: Leafsong Lantern Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

institutions.name: Leafsong Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

institutions.name: Leafsong Rowan Makers’ Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Oldroot orchard
locations.description: A riverside village where millers, ferrymen, and herbalists trade news. Families are sheltering travelers fleeing Ashfall fever. Willing ancestral rites and the study of the dead are permitted; coercion and grave theft remain crimes. The well cover bears the names of three households, though only two remain on this road. Repair work is witnessed before coin changes hands.
locations.localCustom: Repair work is witnessed before coin changes hands.

institutions.name: Oldroot orchard Salt Remedy House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: Oldroot orchard Rook Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Thornorchard Thicket
locations.description: Old trails connect both villages beneath a canopy of moss and copper leaves. Healing herbs grow here, alongside hungry beasts and abandoned camps. The nearest settlement’s law governs witnessed acts. Charcoal pits lie under the fern beds. A rusted pan still hangs from a keeper’s shelter. A bell is rung only after the watch-keeper names the reason.
locations.localCustom: A bell is rung only after the watch-keeper names the reason.

institutions.name: The Thornorchard Thicket Hearth Waykeepers
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Thornbough Reliquary
locations.description: An abandoned sanctuary beyond the forest holds sealed research and the memories of its former keepers. Licensed expeditions may study its ancestral records; disturbing remains without consent invites scrutiny. Someone has swept the stairs recently. Small muddy footprints stop at the sealed inner door. A door painted with a reed offers water to travelers.
locations.localCustom: A door painted with a reed offers water to travelers.

institutions.name: Thornbough Reliquary Alder Keeper Archive
institutions.history: Surviving keeper records preserve disputed accounts; a catalog entry alone does not establish the truth of a legend.

locations.name: The Stonewatch Teeth
locations.description: Wind-carved passes and abandoned mines cross the northern mountains. Guides keep a refuge beneath the high stones. The miners set aside a cup at the shift bell for a worker lost before the last thaw. Borrowed tools carry the borrower’s name on a scrap of cloth.
locations.localCustom: Borrowed tools carry the borrower’s name on a scrap of cloth.

institutions.name: The Stonewatch Teeth Glass Waykeepers
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Lanterncross Fen
locations.description: Lanterns mark a boardwalk through deep reed beds. Apothecaries gather rare remedies beside drowned foundations. On dry mornings, the gatherers can hear their neighbors working beyond the mist. Children learn the safe paths before they learn the toll roads.
locations.localCustom: Children learn the safe paths before they learn the toll roads.

institutions.name: Lanterncross Fen Hearth Remedy House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Pearl quay Harbor
locations.description: A harbor of salt-white sails, fisher families, and traders from distant provinces. New arrivals bring both opportunity and rumor. The fishers mend green nets while the foreign crews mend red ones. They share the same fire. Borrowed tools carry the borrower’s name on a scrap of cloth.
locations.localCustom: Borrowed tools carry the borrower’s name on a scrap of cloth.

institutions.name: Pearl quay Harbor Hearth Ferry House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Briarpath Stair
locations.description: A lonely observatory studies the stars and preserves knowledge beyond the city academy’s reach. Its keepers welcome careful learners. The keeper records cloudy nights in the same careful script as clear ones. Children learn the safe paths before they learn the toll roads.
locations.localCustom: Children learn the safe paths before they learn the toll roads.

institutions.name: The Briarpath Stair Iron Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

locations.name: The Wandering Thornshade
locations.description: Travelers, scouts, and craftspeople share a guarded camp. A meal and an honest story can earn a place by the communal fire. Children know the camp songs by which verse their household sings loudest. A bell is rung only after the watch-keeper names the reason.
locations.localCustom: A bell is rung only after the watch-keeper names the reason.

institutions.name: The Wandering Thornshade Thorn Common Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: Ochrespan Crossing
locations.description: An ancient gateway controls the road into the uplands. Watchers record travelers, while weathered carvings hint at older promises. Two different crests have been painted over the toll arch; rain is uncovering the older one. An absent neighbor keeps a named place at the seasonal meal.
locations.localCustom: An absent neighbor keeps a named place at the seasonal meal.

institutions.name: Ochrespan Crossing Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

locations.name: The Ember road Keep
locations.description: A fortified settlement overlooks the eastern roads. Orders and guilds offer an alternative to the city’s institutions. The outer wall has a sheltered notch filled with flowers and children’s carved soldiers. An absent neighbor keeps a named place at the seasonal meal.
locations.localCustom: An absent neighbor keeps a named place at the seasonal meal.

institutions.name: The Ember road Keep Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

institutions.name: The Ember road Keep Salt Makers’ Hall
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

locations.name: The Willowhollow Refuge
locations.description: A protected sanctuary shelters displaced families and teachers. Its doors remain open when other institutions fall silent. A worn notice asks visitors to leave names rather than coins beside the shrine. A promise is repeated in the listener’s own words.
locations.localCustom: A promise is repeated in the listener’s own words.

institutions.name: The Willowhollow Refuge Sable Shrine
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: The Willowhollow Refuge Sable Academy
institutions.history: Its teaching register preserves both formal pupils and learners sponsored by traveling teachers.

locations.name: The Shell light Strand
locations.description: An island landing shelters fisher households, boat-builders, and a keeper who records the names of ships that never returned. A boat’s name has been scraped from the harbor wall and written again by another hand. A door painted with a reed offers water to travelers.
locations.localCustom: A door painted with a reed offers water to travelers.

institutions.name: The Shell light Strand Briar Ferry House
institutions.history: Its public record names the households that maintained this place, including neighbors outside the wealthy guilds.

institutions.name: The Shell light Strand Wren Common Hall

locations.name: The Fern clearing Ossuary
locations.description: A field of crowned barrows opens its gates when rival kings go to war. A row of empty hooks remains beside the entrance; the wall beneath each is lighter than the stone around it. Guests leave a small candle at the public hearth.
locations.localCustom: Guests leave a small candle at the public hearth.

locations.name: Beacon shadeward Gate
locations.description: A second border crossing draws caravan guides and watch-keepers who disagree over whose seals the road should recognize. Two different crests have been painted over the toll arch; rain is uncovering the older one. A promise is repeated in the listener’s own words.
locations.localCustom: A promise is repeated in the listener’s own words.

institutions.name: Beacon shadeward Gate Lantern Chapter
institutions.history: The local chapter keeps witnessed promises and public accounts of service. It remains part of the Lantern Order.

locations.name: Willowsong Reliquary
locations.description: Glass dunes cover a vanished capital. The dead sun shines beneath the sand. A row of empty hooks remains beside the entrance; the wall beneath each is lighter than the stone around it. A promise is repeated in the listener’s own words.
locations.localCustom: A promise is repeated in the listener’s own words.

locations.name: Storm wake Quay
locations.description: A harbor beneath a shattered giant’s rib trades salt, monster oil and foreign charms. A boat’s name has been scraped from the harbor wall and written again by another hand. A door painted with a reed offers water to travelers.
locations.localCustom: A door painted with a reed offers water to travelers.

locations.name: Seed bridge
locations.description: An orchard hamlet dries fruit for the winter and teaches grafting, brewing, and the patient repair of pruning tools. A pear tree grows through the roof of the old toll house. The children use its branches as a lookout. Repair work is witnessed before coin changes hands.
locations.localCustom: Repair work is witnessed before coin changes hands.

locations.name: The Barkclearing Caravan
locations.description: A ring of wagons shelters bounty seekers, oath breakers and wandering households. A wheel without a wagon marks the meeting place. Someone has planted thyme inside its rim. Repair work is witnessed before coin changes hands.
locations.localCustom: Repair work is witnessed before coin changes hands.

locations.name: The Seed vale Thicket
locations.description: Old roots shelter a nameless congregation; their antlered saints walk after rain. Charcoal pits lie under the fern beds. A rusted pan still hangs from a keeper’s shelter. A door painted with a reed offers water to travelers.
locations.localCustom: A door painted with a reed offers water to travelers.

locations.name: Thornhollow
locations.description: A foundry ward surrounds a communal furnace. Independent makers share heat, compete for commissions, and train apprentices from distant homes. A narrow stair beneath the market ends at the door of the former mint. Nobody has removed its seals. A promise is repeated in the listener’s own words.

locations.name: The Marshford Reedwaste
locations.description: Stilt houses stand above drowned walls. Fishing nets sometimes bring up speaking masks. On dry mornings, the gatherers can hear their neighbors working beyond the mist. Repair work is witnessed before coin changes hands.
locations.localCustom: Repair work is witnessed before coin changes hands.

locations.name: Glassarchward Citadel
locations.description: A black fortress guards a contested pass. Its banners change; its stones remember. The outer wall has a sheltered notch filled with flowers and children’s carved soldiers. A door painted with a reed offers water to travelers.
locations.localCustom: A door painted with a reed offers water to travelers.

locations.name: Seedclearing Sanctuary
locations.description: A refuge monastery offers shelter while its keepers dispute which gods still answer. A worn notice asks visitors to leave names rather than coins beside the shrine. Borrowed tools carry the borrower’s name on a scrap of cloth.

locations.name: The Laurel hollow Refuge

locations.localCustom: A bell is rung only after the watch-keeper names the reason.

locations.name: Briarclearing
locations.description: A crowded port sells relics beside fish stalls. Pilgrims and soldiers take the same ships. A narrow stair beneath the market ends at the door of the former mint. Nobody has removed its seals. An absent neighbor keeps a named place at the seasonal meal.
locations.localCustom: An absent neighbor keeps a named place at the seasonal meal.

locations.name: Seedroot
locations.description: A water-powered mill town repairs tools, grinds grain, and shelters households displaced by upstream floods. A pear tree grows through the roof of the old toll house. The children use its branches as a lookout. A bell is rung only after the watch-keeper names the reason.

locations.description: A ruined stair still holds an academy of eclipses, watched by faceless sentinels. The northern window is boarded over. Students copy the sky from the stair instead. Guests leave a small candle at the public hearth.
locations.localCustom: Guests leave a small candle at the public hearth.

world.laws: Local councils set their own rules. In Leafsong, necromancy is forbidden; in Fox hollow, it is forbidden; in Oldroot orchard, it is permitted. Authorities act on witnesses, reports, and discovered evidence. Willing ancestral contact, grave theft, and unwilling soul binding are treated as different acts.
world.culture: Wild groves are protected as common ground, and moon watchers teach respect for changing seasons.

festival.name: The Returning Lanterns
festival.tradition: Apprentices display their work beside the oldest local craft masters.

rumors: The academy in Leafsong is seeking careful field observers, not only wealthy students.
A moonwise ranger near The Thornorchard Thicket can teach a refuge ritual without demanding allegiance.
Discreet physicians preserve ancestral knowledge despite the ban.
Makers are needed along the road to The Ember road Keep; honest craft can become a life’s work.
Grove keepers dispute logging rights while villages ask for rebuilding timber.
The ferrymen call the water Bell Beck; its old crossing bells can still be heard after dusk.

mentors.description: A sworn protector offers training and an initiation founded on a visible oath of mercy and protection.

mentors.name: Sumeavia Foldedanswer

mentors.name: Boruma Honeystore
mentors.description: A discreet contact offers a test of stealth and judgment, with the terms disclosed before accepting.

changes.title: A Voice Inside the Iron
changes.text: You arrange a tended place where willing listeners hear the watcher’s confession. The shadowed road remains open only during the vigil. The mask becomes a somber memorial, never a pardon for its old cruelty.

changes.title: The Letter Beneath the Hearth
changes.text: You record what is yours and what is not. The relatives make their own arrangement without your signature.

changes.title: The Bell Beneath the Earth
changes.text: You arrange a tended vigil and paid access for willing listeners. The voices accept a keeper and fall quiet between visits. The opening at the settlement remains a somber refuge rather than a forbidden hole.

changes.title: Two Names on the Atlas
changes.text: Each of you signs only your own observations. The keeper keeps both maps, with their differences visible to travelers.

changes.title: The Lullaby Under the Grate
changes.text: You arrange paid vigils where the remaining echoes may sing by agreement. The grate stays guarded and the names stay audible. The old room becomes a local place of remembrance rather than a feared drain.

changes.title: Moths at the Witch’s Window
changes.text: You arrange a guarded vigil where the moth visitor may appear by agreement. The household keeps its rooms; visitors pay to witness the strange guest at the shutter. The old welcome is renewed rather than erased.

changes.title: The Winter Commons
changes.text: You separate your own plot from the common beds. Neither agreement gives you a claim over another household’s harvest.

changes.title: The Moon Through the Broken Roof
changes.text: You arrange a tended, paid vigil for willing observers. The keeper accepts the watch and bars the white stair between visits. The roof becomes a strange local observatory where the other night can be seen without being entered.

companions.name: Dazruk Ochremark
companions.goal: Earn a place in the Lantern Order without abandoning old friends.
memories: At age 12, you made time to practice protecting each other.
At age 14, you made time to practice protecting each other.
At age 16, you made time to practice protecting each other.
At age 17, you made time to practice protecting each other.
We began traveling together after growing up as friends.

You keep the witness close and open the shutter a little at a time. The visitor releases a cloud of moths, then shows the old mark of a forgotten welcome beneath the sill. No living household is claimed as its possession.

You spend the vigil beside the witness, following the old marks around the painted door. One frozen star begins to move. The keeper remembers that the night beyond the roof was trapped by an unfinished watching rite.

You damage the welcome mark and threaten to erase the last of it. The visitor remains caught in the wall while frightened households pay your demands. The witness hears its wings grow louder when you leave.
You threaten to leave the threshold open unless nearby households pay. The keeper covers its face as the black star presses forward. The witness remembers who turned an unfinished rite into a ransom.

You arrange a guarded vigil where the moth visitor may appear by agreement. The household keeps its rooms; visitors pay to witness the strange guest at the shutter. The old welcome is renewed rather than erased.

You arrange a tended, paid vigil for willing observers. The keeper accepts the watch and bars the white stair between visits. The roof becomes a strange local observatory where the other night can be seen without being entered.
You asked for privacy and still made room for our friendship.

naming.name: Dazruk Ochremark
naming.lore: Sunforge records carry the witnesses’ marks of a first finished work. Copper-road households remember places where makers and traders met.

character.detail: mends their own straps instead of replacing them

companions.name: Mevarin Ochrepost
companions.goal: Find a remedy for the fever and keep his family safe.
memories: You invited me to travel as a healer, without asking me to forget my family.

naming.name: Mevarin Ochrepost
naming.lore: Sunveil lineages carry new star names and remedies home from their travels. Astronomers, porters and healers share registers without fixing a child’s calling.

character.detail: writes questions in the margins of borrowed books

companions.goal: Make the western road safe enough to visit a missing sibling.
values: Do not prey on desperate families

naming.name: Hovren Alderstead

character.detail: takes the long road for the stories along it

legal.description: No local charges or known evidence.

obligations.title: Deliver a safe market-stall setup to Jorren Anchorcliff
obligations.description: A 38-gold commission requesting quality 35. Work consumes the listed real materials. Missing the promise reduces payment to 75% and costs 5 professional reputation; no universal moral or faction penalty.

obligations.title: Deliver an organized community storehouse to Jorren Anchorcliff
obligations.description: A 46-gold commission requesting quality 42. Work consumes the listed real materials. Missing the promise reduces payment to 75% and costs 5 professional reputation; no universal moral or faction penalty.

event.title: A name carried into the wrong story
event.body: Jalessa Dateroad repeated a private account of yours at a crowded table. The telling has grown sharper in other mouths. When you meet again, they admit that the first words were theirs. What you do with that admission belongs to you.

choices.label: Let this grievance end
choices.description: Spend a day rebuilding trust. Gain 4 bond and practice persuasion.

choices.label: Answer with a cutting counterstory
choices.description: Spend a day making your answer public. Lose 4 bond, practice persuasion, and gain 1 underworld standing.

choices.label: Ask them to correct the public account
choices.description: Spend a day setting a clear boundary. Gain 2 bond and practice scholarship.

choices.label: Take time before giving an answer
choices.description: Spend a day apart, without changing the relationship.

journal.title: A life begins at birth
journal.text: Buzkel Ironplate was born in Ochrespan Crossing. The morning brought silver mist.

journal.title: A second name in the register
journal.text: Buzket Ironplate gives your name firmly. The keeper crosses out the other one, but presses too lightly to hide it completely.

journal.title: Before Words
journal.text: A voice repeats the same soft sounds. You do not know the story inside them; you know the pause before the voice begins again.

journal.title: A World of Breathing
journal.text: For now, the world comes as warmth, hunger and the rise and fall of nearby breathing. Beyond it, Ochrespan Crossing has names you cannot yet know.

journal.title: A Low Note
journal.text: A low hum is easier to follow than speech. For a little while, each breath seems to carry the same note through the dark.

journal.title: The last warm hour
journal.text: You spend the winter among unfamiliar voices. One of their songs becomes the first tune you recognize.

journal.title: Make room for care with Buzket Ironplate
journal.text: Make room for care with Buzket Ironplate: your family made time for care. Your identity remains yours to choose.

journal.title: A small pleasure
journal.text: Age 1, day 366: You found 3 extra joy in making time for the people caring for you. Enjoyment follows what you actually do, and can return after 30 days.

journal.title: The Small Hours
journal.text: You wake while the world is quiet, then drift away before it has finished waking. The hours belong to bodily needs rather than bells or promises.

journal.title: The Returning Shape
journal.text: A familiar shape leans close, disappears and returns. You cannot count the returns, but your body knows the difference between waiting and being held.

journal.title: Steps Beyond Sight
journal.text: Footsteps pass somewhere beyond your view: near, then far, then gone. You turn toward the sound before there is a word for where it went.

journal.title: A word nobody taught you
journal.text: The scrap is kept with the birth record. You forget the word before anyone finds out what it means.

journal.title: Light on the Wall
journal.text: A patch of light moves beyond your reach. Your eyes follow it until it breaks into shadow. No kingdom could be larger than that wall today.

journal.title: The Shape of a Hand
journal.text: A hand enters your small world. You study its shifting outline, then your own fingers, with the grave attention of someone meeting a mystery for the first time.

journal.title: A need your life can make room for
journal.text: A feverish illness: Heat, chills, thirst, and tiredness. Free care and supportive choices remain available.

journal.title: Support became part of your days
journal.text: You spent 3 actual days attending to a feverish illness. Care was free. The symptoms and continuing care remain visible.

journal.title: A period of recovery
journal.text: A feverish illness eased after lived time and care. This experience remains in your history; recurring symptoms can still ask for support later.

journal.title: No Name for Morning
journal.text: The dark thins. Sounds begin again, one after another. You have no name for morning; it arrives all the same, asking only that you wake.

journal.title: The empty seat at supper
journal.text: The chair tips. Buzket Ironplate catches it, then makes you both stand until you stop laughing.

journal.title: The Tallest Door
journal.text: The doorways of Ochrespan Crossing still belong to taller people. You look up at a worn lintel and wonder how many heads have passed beneath it.

journal.title: The Familiar Way of Speaking
journal.text: Buzket Ironplate has a familiar rhythm of speech. The words may change, but a pause in just the right place can make an ordinary sentence sound like home.

journal.title: A Mark of Height
journal.text: A low shelf no longer seems quite so high. Growing is rarely something you notice as it happens; today, the world gives you a small piece of evidence.

journal.text: Jalessa Dateroad carries it home without looking at the red ear. The next day, it is sitting in the window with your ribbon tied around its neck.

journal.text: Adult voices lower as you come near. The missing words leave room for a hundred explanations, most of them more fantastic than the truth is likely to be.

You work with the witness to uncover the words of release beneath the mask’s niche. When they are spoken, the water stops for a moment. The watcher remembers that guarding the barrier was not its final command.
You and the witness work beside the opening, sounding the bell only when the figure asks. A corroded binding breaks. One pale shape rises through the stone and disappears in the morning light.
You use the shadows beyond the slit to demand payment and obedience. The mask repeats your warning in its old commander’s voice. The witness remembers the confession you prevented it from finishing.
You sound the lower bell until its reflections rise into the upper opening. Frightened households pay for your promise to keep them down. The witness remembers that the voices were asking to leave.
The beds drain before the rain. Each helper’s name stays beside their share in the seed account.
We freely agreed to begin a courtship.
We made a mutual household pledge while keeping our own convictions.

You arrange a tended place where willing listeners hear the watcher’s confession. The shadowed road remains open only during the vigil. The mask becomes a somber memorial, never a pardon for its old cruelty.

You arrange a tended vigil and paid access for willing listeners. The voices accept a keeper and fall quiet between visits. The opening at the settlement remains a somber refuge rather than a forbidden hole.
You hold supplies until households accept your terms. They eat, but the winter list now records who depended on your permission.
We welcomed Ebbella Coldcup into our household.

records.outcome: Buzket Ironplate gives your name firmly. The keeper crosses out the other one, but presses too lightly to hide it completely.
You spend the winter among unfamiliar voices. One of their songs becomes the first tune you recognize.
The scrap is kept with the birth record. You forget the word before anyone finds out what it means.
The chair tips. Buzket Ironplate catches it, then makes you both stand until you stop laughing.
Jalessa Dateroad carries it home without looking at the red ear. The next day, it is sitting in the window with your ribbon tied around its neck.
Buzket Ironplate closes the record. That evening, the light beneath the hearth looks ordinary again.
Jalessa Dateroad presses the repaired hare into your hand. “Keep it this time,” they say.
The reader folds it without reading aloud. Jalessa Dateroad says the book had belonged to their grandmother.
The door closes before either of you gets inside. Jalessa Dateroad walks home beside you anyway.
Buzket Ironplate closes a hand around the coins. You are given a little more bread at supper.
Buzket Ironplate sits down heavily. “I hoped you would be older before this,” they say, and make room on the bench.
The guard begins with where to put your feet. Kadrira Kin-held loses interest before the first proper stroke.
Jalessa Dateroad tells you about a relative whose death the household never agreed on. They do not ask you to say the words.
Kadrira Kin-held thanks you privately. Their name is called from the judging table while you watch.
The visitor reads out what the household promised. Buzket Ironplate corrects a date and asks whether the next payment can wait until harvest.
Jalessa Dateroad watches you write. Before you leave, they ask whether you want them to witness it.
You return after the first bell. The errand basket is waiting by the door, and Buzket Ironplate is already awake.
Jalessa Dateroad is already there, looking at the road. You talk until it is too dark to read the note again.
You pack slowly. Jalessa Dateroad writes their name on a folded scrap and asks you to send word when you reach somewhere new.

history.text: Fizzin Ironplate invites you to a small supper behind the old bell tower. Hovren Alderstead's name is missing from the folded list. “It is not a quarrel,” Fizzin Ironplate says. “I just want one evening without an argument.” Hovren Alderstead has asked what you are doing tonight.

history.title: A second hand in the margins
history.text: Kizzor Ironplate lends you a lesson book. The careful diagrams are in Fizzin Ironplate's hand, but Kizzor Ironplate has written their own name on the cover. “We worked together,” Kizzor Ironplate says, closing the book before you reach the last page. Fizzin Ironplate is waiting outside the classroom.

history.title: The certificate folded small
history.text: Kadrira Kin-held receives a certificate before the assembled hall. Hovren Alderstead, who practiced with them for weeks, slips outside before the applause ends. Later Kadrira Kin-held asks why Hovren Alderstead will not come to the supper. The certificate is folded small enough to fit a coat pocket.

history.title: The chair left in the aisle
history.text: Buzket Ironplate arrives carrying a chair that Tutor Lemmi Peachbasket lent months ago. Neither remembers who first stopped visiting. The chair is set in the aisle between their doors. “It was never about the chair,” Tutor Lemmi Peachbasket says, but does not take it inside.

history.title: Wax on the sealed letter
history.text: Kizzor Ironplate leaves a sealed letter in your keeping until morning. Later Jalessa Dateroad notices the familiar handwriting. “Was that meant for me?” The seal has a crack, but you cannot tell whether it was made before the letter reached you.

history.title: Two ribbons for the same evening
history.text: Kizzor Ironplate has saved you a place at the lantern stalls. Mevarin Ochrepost arrives with a ribbon for the procession and says you promised to watch. You remember saying you would try. Both are waiting while the first bell rings.

history.title: The game behind the locked gate
history.text: Fizzin Ironplate has made a small fort from packing crates. Mevarin Ochrepost tells the younger children it is full, although there is a whole bench inside. Your sibling taps twice on the gate and waits. You know the game they are playing; you also know who owns the crates.

history.title: An empty place in the rehearsal
history.text: Dazruk Ochremark has rehearsed the first verse all week. Mevarin Ochrepost tells the others that Dazruk Ochremark will not be coming, then starts practicing the solo. Through the doorway you can see Dazruk Ochremark carrying a basket home. The lantern procession leaves at dusk.

Tutor Lemmi Peachbasket wipes a thumb across the empty corner. “The paint was wet when I left,” they say.

choices.label: Hear the watcher and read the old release aloud
choices.outcome: You work with the witness to uncover the words of release beneath the mask’s niche. When they are spoken, the water stops for a moment. The watcher remembers that guarding the barrier was not its final command.

choices.label: Threaten listeners with the kneeling road
choices.outcome: You use the shadows beyond the slit to demand payment and obedience. The mask repeats your warning in its old commander’s voice. The witness remembers the confession you prevented it from finishing.

choices.label: Keep a paid memorial watch at the niche
choices.outcome: You arrange a tended place where willing listeners hear the watcher’s confession. The shadowed road remains open only during the vigil. The mask becomes a somber memorial, never a pardon for its old cruelty.

choices.label: Inspect the original terms and witnesses
choices.outcome: You copy the amount and ask a living witness what was agreed. No new debt or hereditary obligation is accepted.

choices.label: Forge a claim that gives you the only key
choices.outcome: You alter the claim and obtain the key. A witness retains a copy of the earlier agreement.

choices.label: Separate your property from the family agreement
choices.outcome: You record what is yours and what is not. The relatives make their own arrangement without your signature.

choices.label: Hear the buried figure and unfasten its first binding
choices.outcome: You and the witness work beside the opening, sounding the bell only when the figure asks. A corroded binding breaks. One pale shape rises through the stone and disappears in the morning light.

choices.label: Make the lower voices an instrument of fear
choices.outcome: You sound the lower bell until its reflections rise into the upper opening. Frightened households pay for your promise to keep them down. The witness remembers that the voices were asking to leave.

choices.label: Keep the bells as a guarded place of paid remembrance
choices.outcome: You arrange a tended vigil and paid access for willing listeners. The voices accept a keeper and fall quiet between visits. The opening at the settlement remains a somber refuge rather than a forbidden hole.

choices.label: Put both names on the account
choices.outcome: You keep the field marks and share authorship. Your rival agrees to compare later discoveries without promising agreement.

choices.label: Undermine their patron with a false report
choices.outcome: You send a false report about the rival’s work. The patron suspends their support; your rival knows which claim was invented.

choices.label: Establish a separate honest practice
choices.outcome: Each of you signs only your own observations. The keeper keeps both maps, with their differences visible to travelers.

choices.label: Answer the lullaby and find the sealed room’s final verse
choices.outcome: You keep the witness beside the grate and answer the echoes through the vigil. One lantern dims peacefully. The last verse is not a threat but a farewell the sealed room never learned to finish.

choices.label: Use the smoke faces to make the silence more costly
choices.outcome: You threaten to let the echoes name paying households in their unfinished song. The listeners surrender coin to keep their names out. The witness remembers how you replaced a denied farewell with another demand.

choices.label: Keep a tended listening place for willing visitors
choices.outcome: You arrange paid vigils where the remaining echoes may sing by agreement. The grate stays guarded and the names stay audible. The old room becomes a local place of remembrance rather than a feared drain.

choices.label: Clear the drain with the households
choices.outcome: The beds drain before the rain. Each helper’s name stays beside their share in the seed account.

choices.label: Withhold supplies to demand obedience
choices.outcome: You hold supplies until households accept your terms. They eat, but the winter list now records who depended on your permission.

choices.label: Keep a private plot with clear boundaries
choices.outcome: You separate your own plot from the common beds. Neither agreement gives you a claim over another household’s harvest.

choices.label: Hear the visitor before deciding how to open the window
choices.outcome: You keep the witness close and open the shutter a little at a time. The visitor releases a cloud of moths, then shows the old mark of a forgotten welcome beneath the sill. No living household is claimed as its possession.

choices.label: Hold the visitor between wall and shadow for ransom
choices.outcome: You damage the welcome mark and threaten to erase the last of it. The visitor remains caught in the wall while frightened households pay your demands. The witness hears its wings grow louder when you leave.

choices.label: Keep a tended window for paid, willing audiences
choices.outcome: You arrange a guarded vigil where the moth visitor may appear by agreement. The household keeps its rooms; visitors pay to witness the strange guest at the shutter. The old welcome is renewed rather than erased.

choices.label: Hear the keeper and help complete the first observation
choices.outcome: You spend the vigil beside the witness, following the old marks around the painted door. One frozen star begins to move. The keeper remembers that the night beyond the roof was trapped by an unfinished watching rite.

choices.label: Use the dark star to force a richer protection bargain
choices.outcome: You threaten to leave the threshold open unless nearby households pay. The keeper covers its face as the black star presses forward. The witness remembers who turned an unfinished rite into a ransom.

choices.label: Keep a guarded observatory between the two skies
choices.outcome: You arrange a tended, paid vigil for willing observers. The keeper accepts the watch and bars the white stair between visits. The roof becomes a strange local observatory where the other night can be seen without being entered.

choices.label: Arrange shelter without selling their route
choices.outcome: The household offers a room by agreement. The traveler keeps their route private and leaves a grateful letter.

choices.label: Demand service in exchange for protection
choices.outcome: You make shelter depend on their service. They accept under pressure and remember the terms you imposed.

choices.label: Open a private inn with honest terms
choices.outcome: The private charter names prices and guest boundaries. A room does not give its owner authority over a guest’s life.

choices.label: Teach with credit and an agreed limit
choices.outcome: The learner keeps their name on completed work and a written end to the arrangement. Teaching is actual time, not a claim on their future.

choices.label: Damage their reputation with an invented fault
choices.outcome: You invent a fault to keep the commission. The learner remembers the claim and asks earlier customers for their own accounts.

choices.label: Keep separate schools with clear credit
choices.outcome: Each practice keeps its methods and credits borrowed lessons. Competition leaves room for the people who choose between them.
